title: KMS state uniqueness and phase transitions in localized Bost-Connes systems: from Chebotarev density to the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture
description:
For a number field K and an arbitrary set S of finite primes we classify the KMS states of the S-local Bost-Connes system A_{K,S}, unconditionally, for every inverse temperature beta > 0. The KMS_beta simplex is affinely isomorphic to Prob(G_S / Xi_beta^perp), where the symmetry group G_S is an extension of the subgroup of the narrow class group generated by S by U_S / closure(O_{K,+}^x), and Xi_beta is the group of characters chi with sum_{p in S} N(p)^{-beta} |1 - chi(Frob_p)|^2 finite. Uniqueness thus holds exactly when, for every nontrivial finite abelian L/K unramified outside S and infinity, the primes of S not splitting completely in L have divergent beta-weighted sum. For S the set of all primes this is Chebotarev density, and at beta = 1 it is the non-vanishing L(1,chi) != 0 of Hecke and Landau; the theorems of Bost-Connes and of Laca-Larsen-Neshveyev are the case S = P_K.

The criterion refutes the natural expectation that divergence of the partition function forces uniqueness. We exhibit S with zeta_{K,S}(beta) infinite, and with the parameter subgroup dense in G_S, whose KMS_beta simplex is a segment at every beta > 0, the two extreme states separated by an explicit pointwise invariant whose almost-everywhere definedness is a Borel-Cantelli condition. Density asks for one prime detecting a character; uniqueness asks for their beta-weighted abundance, and the two separate by a Kakutani dichotomy.

Two further mechanisms are isolated. Over a field of narrow class number greater than 1 the Hilbert class field supplies obstructing characters that are everywhere unramified, impossible over Q. And beta -> Xi_beta is nondecreasing, so systems with any prescribed finite number of phase transitions exist. Finally, for Brun-summable S of critical exponent 1 the partition function is finite at the critical point, so the symmetry-broken phase is closed, the opposite of the classical system.

This record archives the LaTeX source of the paper together with the verification suite, the data it produces, and the figure-generation code. The verification scripts perform finite checks: they can refute a claim but never prove one.

Unrefereed preprint. Theorem 5.5(2),(3),(5) are conditional on a Hardy-Littlewood-strength lower bound for the Sophie Germain primes and are labelled as such in the text; Remark 4.18 notes that the description of G_S as a topological group, though not the criterion itself, is entangled with Leopoldt's conjecture. No priority check against the literature on KMS states of semigroup and groupoid C*-algebras has been completed, and the bibliography has not been independently verified.
notes: Foundational paper of a series on localized Bost-Connes systems; Papers I-XXV are in preparation and will be deposited separately.
